A source guide for a deeper dive.This entry provides a brief orientation and an organized reading path. A comprehensive deep dive has not yet been completed. Follow the annotated sources and distinguish primary community accounts from outside reference material.
01

Identity and homelands

Maya is an umbrella identity encompassing many living peoples, languages, communities, and political histories across Mesoamerica.

Read the sources [1] National Museum of the American Indian

02

Historical context

Smithsonian’s Living Maya Time connects ancient intellectual traditions with present-day Maya voices, rather than treating Maya history as a vanished civilization.

Read the sources [1] National Museum of the American Indian

03

Living communities and further study

ALMG’s community directory opens routes to specific language communities. Study Itza’, Ixil, Mam, K’iche’, Mopan, and other peoples separately as well.

Read the sources [2] Academia de las Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala

Suggested reading and supporting references

These collections preserve links from supplied studies and further research leads. The collection notes explain their provenance and review status. Links already used above point to their source cards. Supporting references and unread leads are excluded from the substantive inspected-source count.

Maya history, culture and timeline · 25 links

Owner-supplied overview of the many Maya peoples, languages and historical periods. Linked to the broad Maya reading entry; individual Maya communities are not interchangeable. Bibliography descriptions and access statements are supplied by the study and require original-source review.
